item.text: {"summary":"The forecast is structurally coherent and uses the correct target, but its May-specific upward adjustment and interval justification need stronger, explicitly evidenced support.","requiredFixes":[{"rubricItem":"update","severity":"warning","summary":"The move from the 6.752 million November 2025 initial print to a 6.840 million May 2026 forecast is attributed to “ordinary seasonal/enrollment recovery” without any cited May-seasonality history or current enrollment evidence.","actionRequested":"Either add official same-month or month-to-month historical evidence supporting the recovery adjustment, or describe the estimate as a persistence-based judgment and reduce/remove the unsupported seasonal component."},{"rubricItem":"interval","severity":"warning","summary":"The 80% interval is obtained from the elicited ladder, but the rationale only says its span is “anchored” in three observations and does not quantify realized first-print or month-to-month variation.","actionRequested":"State a concrete uncertainty basis for the ladder width, such as a defined historical sample and observed dispersion/range, or explicitly explain how administrative first-print uncertainty determined the 6.75–6.95 bounds."},{"rubricItem":"resolver","severity":"warning","summary":"The resolution rule is nearly aligned but omits the canonical fallback to the latest-month table that first includes May 2026 and the explicit 0.001-million rounding instruction.","actionRequested":"Use the ledger resolver text verbatim or add the latest-month-table fallback and round-to-0.001-million requirement."}],"optionalSuggestions":["Explicitly label the persistence prior as the time-series model choice, rather than leaving that inference implicit.","Add a direct official URL or document identifier for the release-calendar evidence."]}
